extra: Unpacked 5,846-byte title tune driver and score.
Title colour nybbles and background byte used by $AE1D.
Tape record 448, the latter part of the packed title tune.
Relocated G-LOADER program and embedded tune data.

comments.text: Leading zero byte of the unpacked music image. The initialization and tick vectors begin at $1001 and $1004.
The timer setup calls this jump vector once to initialize the unpacked SID player at $1055 before IRQ playback begins.

Run the four audio update routines. Every time $A3 expires, advance the song index by two and let $16DA handle reaching the $40 boundary. Finish by writing the SID mode and volume byte with volume fifteen.
Immediate interval at $1014. The sequencer reloads $A3, then advances the event index by two.
Immediate comparison at $101E. At index $40 or above the sequencer calls $16DA before decoding the next event.
Immediate operand of $1028. A zero interval selects the fixed-volume path at $104C, while a nonzero interval leaves the countdown and fade active.
Immediate operand of $1031. When the interval at $03BA expires, the fade path at $1035 reloads the interval and decrements this operand before composing the low four bits of SID volume in $D418.
Immediate value of the ORA at $1050. The fixed path uses this to set full volume before joining the write to $D418.
Clear the first 24 SID registers and initialize the working areas at $033C and $A3. Select the first order entry, then reset the per-pattern byte index and ticker for playback.
Read the three active flags at $0397–$0399 and call $10A7 for each active channel with its SID register base in X and channel number in Y.
Immediate operand at $1089. The update at $108B passes it to $10A7 with the voice-one index.
Immediate operand at $1097. The update at $1099 passes it to $10A7 with the voice-two index.
Immediate operand of $10A5, which supplies the third voice's update value before falling through to $10A7.
Compare a voice's current and target frequency words. Apply the per-channel step until the difference is smaller than the step, then copy the target to the SID register pair.
Invoke $1182 for each channel whose timer-control byte at $039D–$039F is nonzero.
Update the channel count in $039A,X. When it borrows, mask the control at $039D,X and rotate its carry into the channel state at $03A3,X.
Track the software counters at $03A6 and $03A7. Decrement the active step count and use its control bits to change the filter-frequency word at $C9/$CA.
Immediate operand of $120D, loaded from $038A by the filter setup. The sweep compares it with the high cutoff accumulator before choosing the subtraction path.
Immediate operand of $121A. The value is shifted left four times before subtracting it from the low part of the cutoff accumulator.
Check bit 5 of the filter control operand. When set, load a cutoff and envelope parameters from $0386–$038B, then clear the low cutoff byte at $D415.
Immediate operand of $1231, set by the filter update from $038B. Bit 5 selects loading the new cutoff and sweep parameters.
Decrement the filter step counter and add a signed step to the software cutoff at $C9/$CA. Write the updated two bytes to $D415 and $D416.
Copy filter routing and mode from $0385 and $0384. If the voice mask in A intersects $038B, branch to install the new cutoff and sweep settings.
Run the pulse-width path for each of three voices with its seven-register SID stride, choosing rising or falling movement from the per-voice counters.
Decrement the selected voice's rising pulse-width count, add its step to the software width and update the low SID pulse-width byte. Carry into the high byte if needed.

If its falling count is active, subtract the step from the voice's pulse-width word and write both parts to the SID. When the count is exhausted, use control bit 4 to reload the paired pulse-width counts.
If the control has bit 6, initialize the voice's waveform sequence index and store the sequence selector. The shared path increments a running index and selects one of eight entries.
High bytes of the title SID frequency words, indexed by the selected note in the pattern decoder.
Low bytes paired with table $1363. The player adds its current offset before installing the final frequency word.
Load the alternate control byte from $0344 and enter the common voice-one SID control write at $14FE. The next JMP at $1427 enters the event bookkeeping directly.
Read the current pattern pair through $A5/$A6 at the advancing position in $AD. Branch for zero pitch or $80 control, otherwise select instrument parameters and update the first voice.
Writable operand in the first voice's note calculation, set from $180A. The surrounding code selects SID pitch from the two frequency tables and updates this voice's note and gate state.
Clear the gate bit in the previous control value before writing voice one's ADSR. Load the frequency pair $B4/$B5 and apply the new control from $033C.

Immediate operand of $14D9. The following code clears the previous gate on $D404, copies attack and sustain and the frequency to the voice-one registers, then writes the new control byte to both SID and this operand. The following block fetches the voice-two pattern event.
Writable operand in the second voice's parallel note calculation, set from $1886. The result is installed in the voice-two state and SID register path.
Release voice two through $D40B, write its ADSR from $0355/$0356 and then load the next pitch from $BB/$BC and the control from $0354.

Immediate operand of $15C1. The following code clears the previous gate on $D40B, updates the corresponding voice-two envelope and pitch registers, then saves the new control byte here. The following block fetches the voice-three pattern event.
Writable note offset for the third voice, set from $1902. This voice has its own state bytes and follows the same note and control fields.
Release voice three, install its ADSR and frequency and reapply the control value. Save that value into the immediate operand for the next update.
Immediate operand of $16A9. The following code clears the previous gate on $D412, loads the voice-three envelope and pitch, writes the new control byte and keeps a copy here for the next event.
Advance the order index in $AE. At index $1E set $1000 to $FF and wrap to the start, which lets the title input loop continue when the tune finishes.
Load four pattern/settings pointers from the split tables. Copy the per-order transpose and instrument-base fields, then use the settings block to set the ticker period and pattern span.
Mask the instrument control from $A4 and look up its template offset. Copy 16 primary bytes to $033C and, unless the next byte is $FF, eight further bytes to $038B. Return the masked pitch in X.
Copy 16 instrument bytes through the pointer at $B0 to $033C, then advance the source to examine the following filter settings.
Low operand of the indexed store at $1795. The loop copies the 16-byte instrument record through $B0, then advances the pointer to the filter record.
A leading $FF means retain the current filter settings. Otherwise copy eight bytes to $038B, then return the note index masked to seven bits and the gate-control test.
Starting offsets used by the instrument-template copier at $176F.
31 low bytes of the first voice pattern pointers. $16E8 places the selected value at $A5.
Matching high bytes for the first voice pointer at $A6.
Per-order adjustments patched into the first voice's pitch path at $1447.
Per-order offsets copied to $03CA for the first instrument selection.
31 low bytes of the second voice pointers, copied to $A7.
High bytes paired with $1848 at $A8.
Per-order adjustments patched into the second voice's pitch path at $152F.
Per-order offsets copied to $03CB.
31 low bytes of the third voice pointers, copied to $A9.
High bytes paired with $18C4 at $AA.
Per-order adjustments patched into the third voice's pitch path at $1617.
Per-order offsets copied to $03CC.
31 low bytes of the settings pointer loaded into $AB. All nominal entries select the settings block at $253E.
Matching high bytes copied to $AC by the order loader.
First 16 pattern records of 64 bytes each, including the all-zero wait pattern at $197E. The first voice order table references repeated and transposed entries in this region.
Three 64-byte records beginning at $1D7E and $1DBE, then the final common pattern at $1DFE.
Fixed 64-byte records at $1E3E and $1E7E appear in the second voice order table. Later records in the block contain the third voice's early positions.
Sixteen consecutive 64-byte patterns from $203E. The third voice repeatedly selects $207E and $20BE before progressing through the entries beginning at $217E.
Four consecutive 64-byte patterns used by the second voice order table in the second half of playback.
Settings supplied to every order entry. The order loader takes its ticker period from byte two, its pattern length from byte three and volume-control fields from the following bytes.
The instrument records selected by $176F. The copier transfers the first 16 bytes to the common parameter work area and reads an optional extension.
Colour attributes copied four pages at a time to $D800–$DBFF, starting at the end of the title's 1,000 screen attribute cells. The background colour follows at $6710.
Second page of colour attributes. The indexed loop in $AE1D copies these bytes to $D900–$D9FF.
Third page of title colour attributes, copied by $AE1D to $DA00–$DAFF.
Final title colour cells copied to $DB00–$DBE7 before the background-colour byte at $6710.
Source for the global bitmap background colour written to $D021 once the attributes are installed.
Tape record 448 supplies the latter segment of the title music stream. The loader appends it at $4522 after copying the first $0522 bytes from $B011.
A packet boundary in the appended stream. The packet decoder's next output is written at $18CA.
Packet boundary whose expanded bytes begin at $1CB5 in the music driver's image.
The packet beginning here contributes bytes starting at $2149 after decompression.
Closing set of packets whose output begins at $25FE. The zero control at the end of the stream terminates the decode after $26D5.
Eight four-byte records containing two little-endian offsets relative to $8000. $A9AB uses four times the selected speech number to fetch the two offsets.
First packed speech bytes following the descriptor table. Descriptor zero starts here, and descriptor one begins at offset $00A8.
Encoded speech bytes at offset $03E6. This offset appears as the second word of descriptor five; the title playback selects descriptors two and three.
Last 26 bytes of the packed speech interval leading up to its next listing boundary at $8800.
Encoded bytes at offset $0800 from the speech bank. They follow the early descriptor intervals and are traversed by the driver's patched pointers.
Packed speech stream bytes at offset $0C00 within the 5,280-byte record, preceding the higher endpoints in the descriptor table.
Final $04A0 bytes in the tape speech record at offset $1000, still in its encoded form.
Last 160 bytes of record 468, following its first five 1,024-byte groups.
Jump into the two-item sequence at $AA00. The loader calls this after setting up the multicolour title picture.
The control entry dispatches to $A92F, which uses A for the speech-item selection or a control request.
Take a byte from the patched source, shift it and write SID volume. A descending count determines when to advance to another source byte and when to switch to the second NMI handler.

Low operand of the absolute load at $A584. The forward NMI writes the shifted sample to SID volume, acknowledges CIA2 and advances this operand until the forward count expires. It then copies the position to the return-phase load and selects $A5A4 as the next NMI.
Output the shifted byte through $D418 while moving the patched pointer backward. Depending on the flags it either switches NMI entries or exits playback.
Low operand of the absolute load at $A5A5. The backward phase decrements it until $AE expires, then selects the constant-volume phase if $AF is nonzero or advances the speech state directly.
Output the shifted amplitude constant at $A5C6, acknowledge CIA2 and count down the hold interval in $AF. For a remaining interval, switch the NMI vector to $A5D9.
Acknowledge CIA2 and continue decrementing $AF without another SID write until the hold interval is over.
Stop CIA2 timer B via $DD0F, restore SID volume to seven and acknowledge CIA2 before returning.
Save A for the NMI path that reaches the state advance directly from the hold counter.
Install the next NMI entry from $A9F1 and restore the wave position and counters. Increment the repeat counter and branch to refill the wave or advance the segment.
Low operand of the JMP at $A610. The target at $A639 updates the current wave, while the branch at $A60E enters $A613 when the repeat counter wraps.

Preserve X and Y, advance the segment count and request another descriptor if the count wraps. Reset the repeat counter and arm the appropriate continuation before restoring the interrupted registers.
First operand of the call to $A67B. After choosing the stop continuation, the NMI restores Y, X and A before returning.
Restore A and return from the preceding NMI path.
Preserve X and Y, compare the requested and current wave positions and rebuild the wave buffer if they differ. Update the speech wave, restore registers and return from the interrupt.
Subtract the step at $A9F9 from the forward count and add it to the wave position. When the count equals $10, keep the half-buffer select bit and reload the forward count.
Set $A9F1 to the low byte of NMI entry $A5E1 so the next wave transition can stop the timer.
Set $A9F1 to the low byte of NMI entry $A5C3 and set the hold count to $80.
Transfer to the one-bit wave decoder at $A873.
Transfer to the wave reuse path at $A8E3.
Decode packed two-bit samples and join the shared wave update.
Decode the first packed amplitude and fall through to the shared wave update.
Inspect the mode held at $A6B7. Either toggle the half-buffer select and install the current position or refresh the wave positions before updating the wave.
Read the next four-byte segment through $A5. Turn its length and mode flags into NMI counters, then choose a path to rebuild or reuse a wave in page $08.
Writable immediate byte of the entry at $A6B6. The mode path reads its high bits to select the wave refill behaviour.
Four starting wave lengths $08, $10, $18 and $20. The mode at $A72B indexes the table and sets $A9F3.
Store the segment's mode byte and configure the NMI path to reuse the previous wave before advancing the segment pointer.
Build four amplitude bytes per packed sample byte. Look up each two-bit unit in the wave table selected by the low bits, storing the result in page $08.
Reload the packed wave byte using a patched immediate operand. Isolate successive two-bit values and write their mapped amplitudes into page $08.
Immediate operand of $A7A2. The decoder reuses the packed source byte for the remaining two-bit samples, then increments the source pointer and checks the destination index.
Immediate operand of the CPX at $A7D4. The two-bit decoder keeps consuming source bytes until X reaches this limit.
Three four-entry amplitude tables selected by the decoder. Their entries are written to the wave buffer before the playback interrupt reads them.
Add the current count to the end index, extract the first amplitude from the packed high bits and write it into the wave buffer at $0800,X.
Immediate operand of the CPX at $A818. The wave refill at $A7FE repeats until X reaches this index.
Advance the current segment count. Use the signed delta at $A9FD to change the amplitude until that count wraps, then consume a new two-byte segment and look up the next delta.
Sixteen signed deltas used by $A84F. The step comes from the low nybble of the segment control byte.
Start the one-bit wave refill by writing either $0E or $10 according to the first bit, then continue through the following packed units.
Immediate operand of the CPX at $A8AA. The one-bit refill at $A899 repeats until X reaches this index.
Shift four packed bits from A and write amplitude $0E or $10 into successive page-$08 bytes.
Complete one amplitude store, then shift two successive bits out of Y. Append $0E for a clear bit or $10 for a set bit and advance X.
Set the new wave positions and mask the stream byte before switching to the two-bit wave lookup.
Update the source and destination operands of a page-$08 wave copy and rebuild the appropriate half of the wave buffer.
Low operand of the first indexed wave read at $A917. Its value selects where this interpolation run starts reading.
Low operand of the ADC at $A91B. The two source reads feed a carry-aware average for the interpolated wave.
Low address byte of the store at $A91F. $A914 patches the starting position before the loop writes the rounded average of two wave-buffer reads.
The values $FF, $FE and $FD select status, stop and pointer-patch paths. Other inputs prepare a speech item and start CIA2 timer B if bank and timer status allow it.
Return $80 when the processor port makes I/O unavailable. Otherwise return bit zero from CIA2 timer B's control register.
Stop CIA2 timer B by writing $90 to $DD0F and return its status through the shared query.
Store X and Y as the two pointer bytes at $A9FE/$A9FF, then return the current voice status.
Start CIA2 timer B with latch $0064 and enable its interrupt through $DD0D.
Set initial page-$08 decode control, clear waveform counters to their starting values and install the beginning NMI vector.
Multiply the selected item number by four and add the pointer-table base. Read pairs of encoded word offsets relative to the bank into the associated voice stream pointers.
Six-byte identifier consisting of the letters PTR and three spaces, immediately before the descriptor parser's live state.
Low byte of the next NMI entry installed at $A5F5.
Wave position loaded into the forward sample address by $A5FB.
Count copied into both the forward and backward NMI counters.
Hold count copied into $AF by $A608.
Segment counter advanced by $A617. A wrap selects a new descriptor.
Reload value for the repeat counter at $A9F7, derived from the second descriptor byte.
Wave repeat counter. A wrap branches from $A60E to the segment update.
Saved wave count reloaded by $A673 when the count at $A9F3 reaches $10.
Wave position step derived by shifting the saved count right three times at $A708–$A70A.
Saved wave position compared with the current $A9F2 before the repeat path refills the buffer.
Counter advanced by $A81D. Its wrap selects the next two-byte amplitude update record.
Current amplitude before the right shift that sets the NMI hold count.
Signed amplitude step selected through the 16-entry table at $A863.
Low byte of the speech resource base, set by the caller through $A968.
High byte of the speech resource base, paired with $A9FE.
Request speech item two, poll its status until playback stops, then wait for a raster delay and repeat with item three. Exit when the item index reaches four.
Scratch index initialized to two by $AA00 and incremented until it reaches four after two utterances.
Nine zero bytes immediately before the graphics-data suffix. The corresponding bytes of record 267 differ only in the final byte, which is $80 in that record.
Duplicate graphics data matching record 267 at the same offset within the load. The 160-byte match covers two whole 64-byte sprite slots at resident $C500–$C57F and the first half of the next slot.
Final 30 bytes of that duplicate graphics data, matching resident $C582–$C59F.
Jump to the presentation bootstrap at $AC26 after the first cassette stage has put G-LOADER at its relocated address.
Seven five-byte entries used by $AF19. Each has a packed three-digit decimal tape name, destination pointer and a fifth byte that the cassette routine does not read.
Third decimal digit of the record ID in the first loader descriptor. $AF26 masks it to a nibble and converts it to the tape name digit.
Low byte of the destination address in the first loader descriptor.
High byte of the first destination address, paired with $AC05.
Five-byte records following the first entry at $AC02. $AF19 selects a record with X, reads its destination word and converts the three packed decimal name digits for the tape search.
Copy the bootstrap upward by $0C40, working backward. Fetch the presentation records, build the title image and play voice and music before polling for input or continuing the load.
Read CIA1 port A and then select all keyboard rows before reading port B. Continue once there is input or the music-player flag at $1000 changes.
Silence the title SID driver, wait for the raster transition and load the shared graphics and main program. The final transfer is JMP $0880 at $ACFD.
Wait for the raster high bit to clear. Use a descending target derived from the current raster line for 60 wait iterations.
Check both joystick ports' low five bits, and scan all keyboard rows if neither stick has input. Return Z set for no input.
Low byte of the source address at $AD46. The copy advances it and compares the resulting pointer against $5F40.
High byte of the source operand at $AD46. The bitmap copy increments it when the low byte wraps.
Low byte of the destination address at $AD49. $AD4F advances it and the wrap advances the two high address bytes.
High byte of the destination operand at $AD49. The bitmap copy increments it when the paired low byte wraps.
Copy the bitmap's attribute planes, then reveal selected picture cells in a shifting feedback sequence. Calling the input test during the reveal gives the player a shortcut to the direct copy.
Draw the position in $D4 and $D5 when X is below 40 and Y below 200. Shift the three-byte state and apply feedback when carry is set. Repeat until the state returns to one.
Convert X and Y to source and destination offsets, then merge alternating multicolour pixel-pair masks with the bitmap at $E000.
Use X parity to choose a nibble mask at $AEE5, retain that half of the source at ($FE), then OR it into the destination at ($FC).
Copy screen attributes from $5F40 and colour nybbles from $6328, each in four interleaved pages. Set the background from $6710.
Clear 32 pages starting at $E000 while preparing the bitmap.
Select the $C000 VIC bank. Turn on multicolour bitmap layout with screen attributes at $C000 and bitmap at $E000.
Read the packed image from $1000 and expand to $4000. A nonzero control below $80 specifies literal bytes; a high-bit control repeats the following byte. A zero control ends the stream.
Continue the packet decoder with a literal count taken from the positive control byte.
Store A through the destination pointer and advance the pointer to the next output byte.
Read A at the source pointer and advance the pointer to the next input byte.
Switch to the game's I/O-visible memory map, increment border colour and transfer to the KERNAL NMI continuation at $FE2F.
The two masks $F0 and $0F for the colour attribute merge at $AE15, indexed by X parity.
Low byte of the first bitmap row offset. Each following little-endian entry advances by 320 bytes.
Remaining little-endian row offsets from the table that starts at $AEE7. Successive offsets add 320 bytes, the stride of a 40-cell bitmap row.
Read the load destination and three decimal nibbles from the resource entry selected by X. Convert them to PETSCII and jump into the cassette reader at $BE00.
Mask to one nibble and add PETSCII zero.
Store the source pointer in $7E/$7F, with its low byte in Y and high byte in X.
Store the output pointer in $80/$81, with its low byte in Y and high byte in X.
Copy X pages plus Y bytes from ($7E) to ($80), moving high bytes downward as the descending index crosses pages.
Assemble the split packed stream at $4000 by copying $0522 bytes from $B011 followed by record 448's $0D20 bytes from $7000.
Set packed input to $4000 and output to $1000 and run the shared packet decoder.
Install hardware IRQ $AFE6, disable VIC interrupt sources, and enable CIA1 timer A with latch $4625. Initialize the SID player before permitting interrupts.
Save A, X and Y, acknowledge the CIA1 interrupt and call the SID update vector at $1004 before restoring registers and returning.
Write the processor direction byte into all three SID voice control registers, stop CIA1 timer A and acknowledge its interrupt.
High operand of the third SID control store at $AFFD. The shutdown path then stops CIA1 timer A and clears and acknowledges its interrupt.
First $0522 bytes of the unpacking stream. $AF79 copies them ahead of tape record 448 before expanding the music at $1000.
Packet boundary in the packed head at which the next output address is $1363, the start of the decoded frequency lookup.
Beginning of the all-zero area after the packed music head, retained in the G-LOADER record after relocation.
Second $0400-byte section of the loader's zero-filled gap between the packed tune and the cassette reader.
Last $CD zero bytes preceding the loader entry at $BE00.
Entry jump for both presentation and resident calls. The target at $BECC sets up the reader for the three decimal filename bytes and destination already in zero page.
Low target byte of the entry JMP at $BE00, which dispatches into the tape reader setup at $BECC.
Sample and restart timer A on a tape pulse. Shift the selected timer bit into $90, then invoke the current byte parser when the shift register completes a byte.
Read CIA1 timer A high, restart the timer and transform the measured width into a carry bit shifted into $90. When the sentinel bit falls out, jump through the patched byte handler at $BE1B.
Low operand of the JMP at $BE1B. The sync-byte handler switches between entries $BE29 and $BE34 as it seeks two successive $20 bytes before the block marker.
Patch the byte-handler target and exit through $BE1E. The path from $BE3C restores the first sync handler when the marker is neither $20 nor $FF.
Compare successive bytes against the padded name at $BF38 and count mismatches. After 16 bytes, either read the matched header or return to sync detection.
Store four header bytes by advancing the operand at $BE73. Compute the recorded length from the two header words and add it to the caller's destination to get the end pointer.
Zero-page destination operand of $BE72. It advances through $91–$94 to fill the two header words before the reader installs the main payload handler.
Patch the store pointer operand at $BE73 and the IRQ dispatch operand at $BE1C. Copy the start address into $91/$92 and add it to the length to make the end address at $93/$94.
Temporarily bank out I/O, write a byte at the load pointer and advance it. Compare the pointer with the calculated end and switch to the tail parser when the requested length is reached.
Blank the screen, turn on the datasette motor and prepare the padded filename. Mask other interrupts, install the pulse IRQ and wait for its completion flag before restoring the port and border.
Fill the 16-byte buffer at $BF38 with PETSCII space, copy the three decimal name characters and leave the scan index at three.
Sixteen bytes compared by $BE4A against the incoming block name. The setup path changes the first three positions before the comparison.
Second digit of the 16-byte cassette name at $BF38. The IRQ compares the incoming character to this byte when Y is one.
Third digit and space padding of the sixteen-byte name beginning at $BF38.
Mask both CIAs, stop their timers and disable the VIC IRQ sources while preparing CIA1 for pulse polling.
Wait while the VIC raster high bit is clear, then set bits 6 and 4 of $D011.
Raise processor port bit 5 to turn off the tape motor, then set the display-enable bit in $D011 with its raster-high bit clear.
Clear processor port bit 5 to start the tape motor.
First bytes of the zero-filled gap between the tape motor routine and the callback at $BFF1.
Final 24 zero bytes of the gap ending immediately before the resident callback at $BFF1.
Immediate return when called from resident $0A07 in the cassette build.
Zero bytes between the immediate-return callbacks at $BFF1, $BFF7, $BFFA and $BFFD.
Immediate return at this cassette build's restart callback after the resident loader requests record 490.
Two $FF bytes after the immediate-return callback at $BFFD, ending the relocated loader record.
One byte for each of the 1,000 title bitmap cells. Its two nybbles select two of the multicolour bitmap's four pixel colours.
Screen attribute cells 256–511, copied from $6040 while the title image is prepared.
Screen attribute cells 512–767, copied from $6140.
Screen attribute cells 768–999, the visible tail of the last copied page.
Bitmap character rows zero through two. They contain the upper frame and the first line of the title lettering.
Bitmap cells covering the lower strokes of the title wordmark and the fine diagonal ornament near the upper frame.
Bitmap cells across the top of the tower, below the lettering and above its central facade.
Three bitmap rows through the tower's upper facade. Repeated horizontal runs form its dark and light windows.
Three bitmap rows through the tower's middle and the projecting circular structures.
Bitmap cells showing the underside of the circular structures and lower levels of the building.
Bitmap cells covering the base of the tower, with the start of the foreground and author credit strip.
Bitmap cells containing the lower foreground, converging entry paths, and the bottom of the screen frame.
The final 40 cells of the 8,000-byte bitmap ending at $FF3F.
